summary: Kaohsiung's 2026 programme (公告 2026-03-30, 環保局) paid on paper: scrap an 10+ year old gasoline scooter and buy an electric heavy scooter NT$7,000 (light NT$5,000); buy new without scrapping NT$4,000 (light NT$2,000); low-income households NT$12,000/8,000 and NT$10,000/4,000. The big money was the top-ups: NT$20,000 heavy or NT$10,000 light for ages 18-30, medical staff or parents of school-age children (pick one), plus NT$3,600 or NT$7,200 for battery-rental plans. City-only paper maximum for a heavy scooter was NT$34,200 (our arithmetic; no city-published total). But the bureau's page says the money ran out on 2026-08-11 with NT$0 remaining; applications totalled about NT$81.4M against an NT$80M cap, and over-cap applicants face a lottery. A buyer now should assume no city subsidy, and no 2027 programme is announced. Rules: Kaohsiung household registration, 2026 invoice, plate stays in the city 1-3 years. Previous city-subsidy recipients are excluded. No city gasoline subsidy to net off. Stacking with central subsidies and local parking/charging perks: not found.

findings.subject: Over-budget rule: stop, then public lottery; non-winners get nothing
